test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Mid-Range Full Test - 04
subject: general
question:
In this question, three statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II have been given. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from the commonly facts and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

**Statements:** 

Some flats are apartments.

No apartment is a hall.

Some halls are rooms.

**Conclusions:**

I. At least some rooms are flats.

II. No apartment is a room.

options.text: Both Conclusions I and II are true
Neither Conclusion I nor II is true

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement will be:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7cd4618544af5bc490c84b038c0e6cca022c3d096a266e523f1a35049d418237.png] 

Conclusions:

I. At least some rooms are flats. → False (It is possible but not definite)

II. No apartment is a room. → False (It is possible but not definite).

Hence, the correct should be "**Neither Conclusion I nor II is true**".
